maria: Hey team — customer reporting intermittent SSE stream drop ~45s after connect, then a 401 on reconnect. Request ID from logs: req_9f1c3b2a. Logs show a short TLS rehandshake then 401. Can someone help with a minimal curl repro and what to collect?

maria: logfile excerpt:
```
[2026-01-15T14:22:13Z] INFO connection established request_id=req_9f1c3b2a client_ip=203.0.113.45
[2026-01-15T14:23:00Z] WARN tls: session resumed, new session_id=AB:CD:EF
[2026-01-15T14:23:20Z] ERROR auth: token validation failed request_id=req_9f1c3b2a reason=expired
```

sam: Thanks — please paste the exact curl you used (sanitized). We need a reproducible command with -v and --trace-ascii to capture headers + TLS info. Also include the x-request-id header you saw. If you can, toggle --no-keepalive to see if keep-alive affects it.

alex: Quick checklist for a streaming-auth repro:
- include full headers: Authorization (sanitized), x-request-id, Host, Connection
- add `--http2 --no-keepalive --compressed -v` for better parity
- capture TLS handshake with `openssl s_client -connect host:443 -tlsextdebug -status` if possible

maria: Uploading sanitized curl + capture now. Replacing real key with <REDACTED_KEY>. Using customer's environment behind a proxy. Curl I ran:
```
curl "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>" \
  -H "x-request-id: req_9f1c3b2a" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  --http2 --no-keepalive --compressed -v --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt
```

maria: Uploaded sanitized debug bundle: https://storage.redwood.dev/debug/1765432100-bundle.tar.gz (contains /tmp/trace.txt and stripped logs) @sam @alex :eyes:

ops-bot: debug-bundle-uploader: bundle 1765432100 processed, link https://storage.redwood.dev/debug/1765432100-bundle.tar.gz, redacted keys detected.

ingest-bot: Received request_id=req_9f1c3b2a — correlating with infra logs, span id span_4a8d.

sam: Downloaded the bundle and replaying the curl here. I can reproduce a 401 on reconnect when token rotation happens client-side right at ~45s. Trace shows Authorization header present on initial connect but missing on one subsequent resume attempt (proxy/clt reuses TLS session but not header).

sam: trace snippet (sanitized):
```
> GET /v1/stream HTTP/2
> :method: GET
> :path: /v1/stream
> authorization: ********
< HTTP/2 200
< content-type: text/event-stream
... stream open ...
--- TLS session resumed ---
> GET /v1/stream HTTP/2
> :method: GET
> :path: /v1/stream
> (missing) authorization: <not sent>
< HTTP/2 401
```

alex: Sounds like an edge/proxy issue where the client reconnect used a new HTTP/2 stream without re-supplying the Authorization pseudo-header. Two likely causes: the customer's proxy strips headers on resumed sessions, or their client lib reuses a pooled connection but doesn't attach auth on the follow-up request.

alex: Quick mitigation steps to confirm:
- have customer set `Connection: close` to force full handshake and confirm header sent each time
- or add `--header "authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>"` explicitly per request in repro (curl already does this)
- ask them to test with a direct connection (bypass proxy) or enable proxy logs to show header flow

maria: Ran `Connection: close` variant — no resume observed and no 401 for >5m in our test. Will ask customer to test direct-to-origin.

sam: For eventual fix, eng-runtime should harden edge to reject resumed sessions that drop required auth headers, or emit clearer logs. I'll escalate with the bundle and trace id span_4a8d. Filing internal ticket.

maria: Filing ticket now and attaching bundle. Thanks all :thumbsup:
